Conditions: (1) You count as doing international transport only if you start both reduced rests outside the employer's Member State and outside your country of residence. (2) In any four consecutive weeks you must take at least four weekly rests, and at least two of them must be regular rests of at least 45 hours. (3) Both reductions must be made up with an equivalent rest taken in one block. This compensation must come right before your next weekly rest, and in any case before the end of the third week after the week in question. (4) Your employer must organise your work so you can get back to the operational centre where you are based, or to your home, before that compensated regular rest of more than 45 hours starts. (5) That compensated rest and any regular weekly rest may not be taken in the vehicle. They must be taken in suitable accommodation with adequate sleeping and sanitary facilities, and the employer pays for it.
